note: Repo command guards scan the whole Bash command STRING, so prose ABOUT a command trips them even when nothing is being executed. Hit twice in one session while writing documentation. First: a heredoc appending ledger notes that quoted a whole-workspace doctest invocation was refused by the guard that redirects such invocations to make gate. Second: the same guard fired on a heredoc containing plan text that listed two scoped test commands in one step. Neither command was going to run -- both were being written into a markdown file. The guards are correct about execution and have no way to know the difference. Workarounds, cheapest first: rephrase the prose (say the workspace doctest step rather than quoting the command), or write the file with a file-writing tool instead of a heredoc so the trigger text never appears in a shell command, or set the documented override variable if you genuinely mean it. Worth knowing before you spend three turns thinking your ledger append is broken.
